literal: Not-staying nature-it-has wealth; that if obtained, things-that-abide right-then do.
translation: Wealth is transient by nature. When you obtain it, immediately use it to do things that will last.
modern: செல்வம் நிலைக்காத இயல்பினை உடையது. அதனைப் பெற்றால், பெற்ற அப்பொழுதே நிலைத்து நிற்கும் நல்ல செயல்களைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the fleeting nature of wealth. The word அற்கா means not staying or unstable, describing wealth's natural tendency to vanish. Because wealth can disappear at any moment, the poet advises that the moment one acquires it, they should immediately invest it in அற்குப—deeds of virtue that will endure forever.
